neighbours.label: a demonstrative ('that', 'these') used without pointing at a noun: as a degree word ('that long', 'that much') or in the set phrase 'these days'; demonstratives that determine a noun stay low
fire: I never expected the drive to the coast to take that long.
Honestly, the repairs did not cost that much in the end.
We rarely see snow falling that early in the autumn.
My brother mostly cooks pasta these days because it is quick.
The trail was not that steep once we passed the bridge.
Most of my friends work from home these days.
Nobody thought the river could rise that fast overnight.
The old printer was never that reliable, to be fair.
quiet: I never expected the drive to the coast to take four hours.
Honestly, that repair did not cost us anything in the end.
We rarely see snow falling in the autumn here.
My brother mostly cooks these pasta dishes because they are quick.
The trail was steep, but that bridge made it easier.
Most of my friends work from home on these laptops.
Nobody thought that river could rise overnight.
That old printer was never reliable, to be fair.
